text:
maria: FYI customer (AcmeRetail) on Dedicated eu-west is hitting 401s on the API after SSO redirect. They say it worked yesterday. Attached a simple repro: 

curl -v 'https://private.acme.redwood/api/v1/chat' -b 'rw_sso=eyJhbGciOi...'

response: 401 Unauthorized. Customer insists cookie is present in the request.

kevin: Do we have a gateway-level cookie->auth header rewrite in place for dedicated tenants? Some LB setups convert cookies to Authorization; others drop them. Can you paste the raw request headers the customer captured?

maria: Here are the headers they forwarded from their side (redacted):

Client->LB:
GET /api/v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: private.acme.redwood
Cookie: rw_sso=opaquetoken123; other=1
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0

LB->Gateway (what gateway logs see):
GET /api/v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: private.acme.internal
X-Forwarded-For: 35.23.12.4
X-LB-Session: xyz

(no Cookie header, no Authorization header)

maria: So cookie disappears between LB and our gateway. customer says they recently flipped on a rewrite rule in their GCLB to enable SameSite handling for the cookie — could be related.

noa: GCP L7 + Envoy combo can be finicky. If there's a redirect (http->https or host rewrite) and the LB issues a Set-Cookie then the subsequent request might not include cookie anymore. Also some internal proxies drop Cookie to avoid header bloat. Any chance the LB is terminating TLS and re-issuing requests without forwarding the Cookie header?

kevin: Two quick things to confirm: 1) Does the gateway see the original Host header or a rewritten one? (preserve_host) 2) Do we have an ingress filter that strips Cookie for certain routes? Can you capture gateway request headers with debug logging?

maria: I enabled gateway debug for that tenant and reproduced. From the gateway access log:

[2025-08-12T14:03:12Z] tenant=acmeretail method=GET path=/api/v1/chat src=35.23.12.4 headers="Host: private.acme.internal; Authorization: ; X-LB-Session: xyz" status=401

maria: Looks like Authorization header present but empty, and Cookie missing entirely.

david: If Authorization is present but empty we might have a previous header rewrite/filter that tries to parse cookie -> bearer and failed, leaving an empty header. Do we have a lua filter or envoy config that touches Authorization?

maria: Not in the tenant config we control. Customer confirmed they added a custom header-action in GCLB which 'cleans' cookies and tried to insert Authorization. They might have a buggy template that sets Authorization to blank on missing cookie.

kevin: Ok that matches. Short-term workaround: convert cookie to Authorization at our gateway (defensive) before upstream auth check runs. We can add a small envoy.lua rewrite that extracts rw_sso cookie and sets Authorization: Bearer <token>. Will push as a canary for just AcmeRetail.

kevin: Suggested snippet (testing only):

```
inline_code: |
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local cookie = request_handle:headers():get("cookie")
  if cookie then
    local tok = cookie:match("rw_sso=([^;]+)")
    if tok and tok ~= "" then
      request_handle:headers():replace("authorization", "Bearer " .. tok)
    end
  end
end
```

noa: Use `:replace` not `:add` to avoid duplicate Authorization headers, and run lua in the early filter chain so downstream auth sees a value. Also limit to the tenant route to minimize blast radius.

maria: Is there a suggested rollout command for that? I don't want to touch global gateway config.

kevin: You can deploy as a gateway config canary:

```
rb-cli deploy-gateway-config --file gw-rw-cookie-rewrite.yaml --canary acmeretail
```

where gw-rw-cookie-rewrite.yaml contains the lua filter under http_filters for the gateway and a match rule for tenant "acmeretail" host.

maria: Customer approved canary. Please go ahead.

deploy-bot: Deploy job queued: job-id=gw-deploy-20250812-42 for canary=acmeretail

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: gw-rw-cookie-rewrite v2.1 -> canary=acmeretail (started 2025-08-12T14:15Z, finished 2025-08-12T14:18Z)

maria: I validated with the customer: curl now returns 200 when passing the cookie. They confirmed UI flows work post-SAML. Marking resolved on our side, leaving customer to confirm full rollout.

kevin: Follow-up (postmortem note): we should add a monitoring alert for empty Authorization headers on auth-protected routes and document that LB header templates can result in empty headers; also add a small defensive cookie->auth rewrite option in tenant gateway configs.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a doc + task.

-- end of thread --
